subject: english-literature
title: Fragmentation and Time
welcome_lead: Modernist novels shatter linear time. Examine fragmentation, simultaneity and Bergsonian duration.
meta_desc: Fragmented narrative and time disruption in modernist prose at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have followed modernist time — clock and consciousness pulling apart.

concepts.def: Modernist novels reject continuous narrative for shards, jumps and juxtaposition.
Henri Bergson's distinction between mechanical clock time and lived durée; influential on Proust and Woolf.
Modernism's interest in rendering multiple events occurring at once (Mrs Dalloway, Manhattan Transfer).
Genette's terms for flashback and flash-forward; modernists disrupt chronological order.
Involuntary memory triggered by sensory stimulus (the madeleine in À la recherche du temps perdu).
The chiming of Big Ben punctuates Mrs Dalloway, marking the gap between public clock and private consciousness.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bergson distinguished mechanical temps from lived durée. Modernist novelists privilege duration — time as felt — over the abstract clock.

Eliot's The Waste Land (1922) juxtaposes scraps of myth, slang and song. Dos Passos's U.S.A. intercuts narrative with newsreels.

Form models the fragmentation of post-war experience.
Proust's À la recherche du temps perdu (1913-27) makes involuntary memory a structural principle. The madeleine releases a flood of recollection, restoring the past as present.
